chapter.name: Preamble of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: The text, ingredients, key words, significance, status and amendability of the Preamble.

concepts.name: Text, origin and ingredients of the Preamble
concepts.description: What the Preamble is, where it came from, its present wording and its four ingredients.
concepts.idea: The Preamble is the introduction to the Constitution, based on the Objectives Resolution and amended once in 1976.
concepts.rule: A preamble is the introduction to a constitution and holds its essence; the American Constitution was the first to have one. N.A. Palkhivala called it the identity card of the Constitution. India's Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added three words: Socialist, Secular and Integrity. It declares that We, the People of India, resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and to secure justice (social, economic, political), liberty (thought, expression, belief, faith, worship), equality (of status and opportunity) and to promote fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation, and adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. It has four ingredients: source of authority (the people), nature of the State, objectives, and date of adoption.
concepts.example: The Preamble was called the 'identity card of the Constitution' by N.A. Palkhivala.

concepts.name: Sovereign, socialist and secular
concepts.description: What the three words mean in India's Preamble and how they developed.
concepts.idea: India is an independent State, follows democratic socialism and practises positive secularism.
concepts.rule: Sovereign means India is neither a dependency nor a dominion but an independent State with no authority above it, free to manage its internal and external affairs. Membership of the Commonwealth (1949) and of the UN does not limit this sovereignty, and India can acquire or cede territory. India was a dependency until 15 August 1947, a dominion until 26 January 1950, and became a sovereign republic then. Socialist was added in 1976, but socialist content already existed in some Directive Principles and the Congress adopted the 'socialistic pattern of society' resolution at Avadi (1955). India's socialism is democratic socialism, not state socialism, and favours a mixed economy where public and private sectors co-exist; the Supreme Court said it aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity, blending Marxism and Gandhism with a lean to Gandhism. The 1991 economic policy diluted it. Secular was also added in 1976, though the Court in 1974 said the Constitution-makers meant a secular State, as shown by Articles 25 to 28. India follows positive secularism, in which all religions have the same status and support from the State.
concepts.example: In a theocratic state one religion is declared the state religion; in a secular state the state is neutral.

concepts.name: Democratic and republic
concepts.description: Direct and indirect democracy, the Indian parliamentary democracy, and the meaning of a republic.
concepts.idea: India is a representative parliamentary democracy and a republic with an elected head of state.
concepts.rule: A democratic polity rests on popular sovereignty, the supreme power of the people. Democracy is direct (as in Switzerland, with the devices of referendum, initiative, recall and plebiscite) or indirect (representative), which can be parliamentary or presidential. India has a representative parliamentary democracy in which the executive is responsible to the legislature. Universal adult franchise, periodic elections, rule of law, independent judiciary and absence of discrimination reflect it. 'Democratic' in the Preamble covers political, social and economic democracy. Ambedkar warned on 25 November 1949 that political democracy cannot last without social democracy, and that liberty, equality and fraternity form a union, so no one can be divorced from the others. A democratic polity is either a monarchy (hereditary head, as in Britain) or a republic (head elected for a fixed term, as in the USA). India's republic has a President elected indirectly for five years. A republic also means sovereignty rests in the people and public offices are open to all without a privileged class.
concepts.example: Referendum, initiative, recall and plebiscite are devices of direct democracy.

concepts.name: Justice and liberty in the Preamble
concepts.description: The three forms of justice, distributive justice, and the meaning and limits of liberty.
concepts.idea: Justice is social, economic and political, and liberty is real but not absolute.
concepts.rule: Justice in the Preamble has three forms secured through Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Social justice means equal treatment without distinction of caste, colour, race, religion or sex, and improvement of backward classes and women. Economic justice means non-discrimination on economic grounds and removing glaring inequalities of wealth, income and property. Together social and economic justice give distributive justice. Political justice means equal political rights, equal access to political offices and equal voice in government. The ideal of justice is taken from the Russian Revolution (1917). Liberty means absence of restraints on individual activity while giving opportunities for developing personality. The Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship through enforceable Fundamental Rights. Liberty is not licence and is qualified by limits in the Constitution. The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity come from the French Revolution (1789-1799).
concepts.example: Combining social and economic justice gives what is called distributive justice.

concepts.name: Equality and fraternity in the Preamble
concepts.description: Three dimensions of equality, the provisions that secure them, and the meaning of fraternity, dignity and integrity.
concepts.idea: Equality means no special privileges; fraternity means brotherhood assuring dignity and national unity.
concepts.rule: Equality means absence of special privileges and adequate opportunities for all. The Preamble secures equality of status and opportunity, with civic, political and economic dimensions. Civic equality is secured by Articles 14 to 18. Political equality is sought by Article 325 (no one ineligible for the electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex) and Article 326 (adult suffrage for the Lok Sabha and state assemblies). Article 39 in the Directive Principles secures men and women equal means of livelihood and equal pay for equal work. Fraternity means brotherhood, promoted by single citizenship and by the Fundamental Duty of Article 51A to promote harmony and common brotherhood. The Preamble says fraternity must assure the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation. 'Integrity' was added in 1976. K.M. Munshi said dignity of the individual means every person's personality is sacred. Article 1's 'Union of States' shows that states cannot secede, giving the Union an indestructible nature and the aim of overcoming communalism, regionalism, casteism, linguism and secessionism.
concepts.example: Equal pay for equal work for men and women is secured by Article 39.

concepts.name: Significance, status and amendability of the Preamble
concepts.description: Tributes to the Preamble, the Berubari, Kesavananda Bharati and LIC cases, and the 1976 amendment.
concepts.idea: The Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but not to change its basic features.
concepts.rule: The Preamble embodies the basic philosophy and fundamental values of the Constitution. Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer said it expresses what we had long thought or dreamt. K.M. Munshi called it the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic', Thakur Das Bhargava the soul and jewel of the Constitution, Ernest Barker its 'key-note', and M. Hidayatullah said it resembles the American Declaration of Independence but is more than a declaration. In the Berubari Union case (1960) the Supreme Court said the Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers but is not part of the Constitution. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) it rejected that opinion and held the Preamble is part of the Constitution; the LIC of India case (1995) confirmed it. The Preamble was enacted last, after the rest of the Constitution, to ensure conformity. It is neither a source of power for the legislature nor a limit on its power, and it is non-justiciable. In Kesavananda the Court held the Preamble can be amended under Article 368 but its basic features cannot be altered. It has been amended once, in 1976, adding Socialist, Secular and Integrity; the amendment was held valid.
concepts.example: The Preamble is not enforceable in courts but helps interpret ambiguous Articles.
